papers.title_en: Synergy-Aware Residual Flow Matching for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
papers.evidence: 面向单细胞扰动响应预测的协同感知残差流匹配
papers.tldr: 组合扰动预测中，响应大部分可由单扰动加性效应解释，真正有生物学意义的协同信号藏在较小的非加性残差里，直接生成完整表达谱容易把容量耗在加性成分上。SynGeneFlow 以加性先验为源分布，学习指向真实扰动状态的残差流匹配，并用基因互作掩码和扰动相关形变偏置建模条件耦合。模型还用 MMD 对齐终点与生物残差分布，在遗传/药物扰动基准的多种设置下表现稳健。该工作把流匹配残差化到加性效应周围，为单细胞扰动响应预测提供了更具生物依据的框架。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting single-cell responses to genetic and chemical perturbations is important for understanding regulatory mechanisms and prioritizing therapeutic interventions. Existing methods have made progress by modeling perturbation-conditioned expression shifts with neural networks, graph priors, foundation-model representations, or distributional generative models. However, combinatorial perturbation prediction remains challenging because much of the response can be explained by additive single-perturbation effects, while the biologically informative signal often lies in a smaller non-additive residual induced by perturbation interactions. Directly generating the full post-perturbation expression profile may therefore allocate substantial capacity to the dominant additive component and underemphasize synergy-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{SynGeneFlow}, a synergy-aware flow matching framework that anchors the source distribution at an additive prior and learns a residual flow toward the true perturbed state. SynGeneFlow further incorporates perturbation-conditioned gene interaction modeling, where a static gene-gene mask provides biological structure and a perturbation-dependent deformation bias dynamically modulates gene-gene coupling. To preserve population-level response structure, we align both endpoint distributions and biological residual distributions with MMD-based regularization. We evaluate SynGeneFlow on genetic and drug perturbation benchmarks under observed-single, held-out, and cross-modality settings. The results demonstrate that residualizing flow matching around additive perturbation effects provides a biologically grounded and robust framework for single-cell perturbation response prediction.

papers.title_en: A Pitfall in the Evaluation of Gene Perturbation Models
papers.authors: George Panagopoulos, Saman Omidi, Tsz Pan Tong, Jun Pang
papers.evidence: 基因扰动模型预测转录响应及统一评估
papers.tldr: 基因扰动模型常用不同指标和差异表达基因子集比较，导致评估结论可能不可靠。作者在6个单基因扰动数据集上统一评测8种方法，发现改变Top DE基因数会使基于Precision的排名剧烈波动，胜出方法有86.7%概率改变。进一步揭示将同一预测表达谱复制到细胞行会膨胀显著性，67.1%的扰动-基因对过阈值，即使效应微小。纳入该陷阱后，使用Gene Ontology特征的随机森林总体最佳。
papers.abstract_en: Gene perturbation models aim to predict transcriptional responses to unseen genetic interventions, but comparisons rely on heterogeneous evaluation metrics and differentially-expressed (DE) gene subsets. We investigate the consequences of these choices using eight methods across six single-gene perturbation datasets under a unified evaluation protocol. Varying the number of top DE genes reveals substantial instability in Precision-based rankings, with the winning method changing $86.7\%$ of the time, while rankings based on the rest of the metrics remain comparatively stable. Investigating this discrepancy exposes that repeating a single predicted expression profile across cell-level rows, a standard practice for many methods, can inflate significance estimates and produce excessively large predicted significant-DE sets. Specifically we found that $67.1\%$ of tested perturbation--gene pairs pass the significance threshold despite some of them having minuscule effects. We derive an inflation factor showing that replicated predictions can amplify the standardized Mann--Whitney statistic even after correction for tied ranks, without adding independent information. This artifact changes Precision mainly as the number of DE genes increases because for smaller cutoffs, most of the genes are already significant due to the effect-based ordering. Taking this pitfall into account in our benchmark comparison, we find that a random forest using Gene Ontology features achieves the best overall results.

papers.title_en: Panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes at scale with CellNet
papers.authors: Xiaoqing Lian, Pei Liu, Jiahui Tan, Luoda Tan, Chaoyi Li, Quan Zou, Chen Lin, Xiangxiang Zeng
papers.evidence: 大规模单细胞转录组基础模型，可作为虚拟细胞建模的骨干
papers.tldr: 单细胞转录组蕴含丰富信息，但现有基础模型常只覆盖有限分子层面。CellNet将DNA来源的基因身份与实测RNA表达整合为共享图像表示，并在涵盖2.31亿个细胞图谱、40个物种的大规模数据上预训练。它在稀有群体与条件相关状态识别上表现更优，并保持通用表示竞争力，同时能预测总RNA中编码基因及部分非编码靶标、跨物种靶标和空间谱系模式。该框架为利用更全面的转录组测量解读细胞多样性提供了可扩展方案。
papers.abstract_en: Comprehensively characterizing cellular diversity is critical for understanding tissue development, identifying disease-associated populations and investigating gene programmes linked to specialized functions. Advances in single-cell profiling reveal additional cell-specific transcripts and molecular associations, yet many foundation models represent only a restricted portion of this increasingly rich molecular information. Here we present CellNet, which enables panoramic modelling of single-cell transcriptomes by integrating DNA-derived gene identities and measured RNA expression in a shared image representation. Pretrained on 231 million cell profiles spanning 40 species, CellNet improves rare-population and condition-associated state recognition in evaluated cohorts while retaining competitive general cell representations. It predicts withheld coding-gene expression and selected non-coding targets in total-RNA data, and recovers lineage-specific expression patterns in spatial measurements. Prediction also extends across species, including to targets without expression-pretraining exposure. Its gene representations retrieve known non-coding modules and developmental or neural programmes, including from sparsely detected RNA queries. Together, these results establish CellNet as a scalable framework for interpreting cellular diversity through increasingly comprehensive transcriptomic measurements.
